hero-title: Digital public infrastructure with credible neutrality
hero-description: Explore Ethereum as a public base layer for durable digital infrastructure, including records, credentials, payments, and data exchange.
intro: Identity, payments, records, and data exchange can become foundational public infrastructure. When these systems rely on one operator, that operator can be a single point of failure and control. Ethereum offers a public base layer whose core rules are not owned by a vendor, agency, or company.
neutrality-description: No organization, including the Ethereum Foundation, can unilaterally change the core network rules to favor one participant. A public deployment still relies on applications, integrators, and operators; assess them separately and design alternatives and exit paths.
credentials-description: Allow people to hold and present verifiable claims while minimizing disclosure.
records-description: Create tamper-evident shared history where several parties need to verify data.
payments-description: Coordinate value transfers with clear rules and proportionate privacy.
exchange-description: Publish or prove information without requiring every verifier to depend on one database.
weigh-description: Plan for inclusion, accessibility, privacy, legal duties, key recovery, cost, provider failure, and long-term in-house capability. If a public authority legitimately controls a process end to end and no external party needs to verify it independently, a well-governed conventional system may be better.
